Backed by Naga bodies, Meitei groups hold rally in Imphal for abrogation of SoO truce pact
 Naga civil bodies held marches in Chandel and Senapati districts, supporting the rally by the COCOMI in Imphal; rallies come days after militants ambushed 14 Meitei men and killed three of them, sparking protests in the State
 Updated - October 31, 2026 08:33 pm IST - Imphal 
 PTI READ LATER 
 SEE ALL 
 Remove 
 Thousands of people started their march from Tiddim Ground towards THAU ground in Imphal West district. (Image used for representational purpose only)
 | Photo Credit: PTI
 An umbrella body of Meitei groups held a massive rally in Manipur’s capital city Imphal on Saturday (October 31, 2026) seeking protection for indigenous people and the scrapping of the Suspension of Operations (SoO) agreement with militant groups, demands endorsed by several Naga organisations.
 Naga civil bodies held marches in Chandel and Senapati districts, supporting the rally by the Coordinating Committee on Manipur Integrity (COCOMI) in Imphal. The Naga organisations have also demanded termination of the agreement, accusing Kuki-Zo militant groups of being involved in violence.
 Meitei group rejects Suspension of Operations pact with Kuki-Zo groups in Manipur After ambush
 The rallies came days after militants ambushed 14 Meitei men and killed three of them , sparking protests in the State, which has been plagued by ethnic violence since May 2023.
 Thousands of people, including those belonging to the Naga community, started their march from Tiddim Ground towards THAU ground in Imphal West district as part of the rally organised by COCOMI. Naga apex body — United Naga Council — endorsed the rally.
 Police put up barricades at Keisampat junction, just a few hundred metres from the Lok Bhavan, Chief Minister's Office and the BJP State office, and prevented the rally from moving ahead.
 Participants of the rally held up posters and placards that read ‘Save Manipur’, with demands such as ‘we want peace and justice’ and ‘Abrogate SoO pact’.
 Congress demands Manipur CM’s resignation, fresh polls amid renewed violence ‘Govt. should resign’
 “We seek the resignation of the present government for its failure to protect the lives and properties of the indigenous people of the State. This is a historic rally. People are raising their voice against policies and programmes which are against the indigenous people,” said COCOMI convenor Y. Dhiren.
 A protester said, “After three-and-a-half years of crisis in Manipur, Naga tribes, Meiteis and the native people are coming together to raise their voice against the government for their policies against the indigenous people of the State. We have endured enough pain, loss of lives and property.” “We must fight illegal immigrants and narco-terrorism, and secure our future,” he said.
 In Naga-majority Senapati district, a rally demanded the immediate abrogation of the SoO agreement and the resignation of Deputy Chief Minister Nemcha Kipgen. It was organised by Naga People’s Organisation (NPO), Senapati District Students’ Association (SDSA) and Senapati District Women’s Association (SDWA) in support of the rally called by COCOMI in Imphal.
 New fault lines: On Manipur’s Kuki-Zo–Naga conflict UNC president N.G. Lorho said Nagas across the hill districts had united to defend their ancestral land. “We are the owners and guardians of our land from time immemorial. We will not surrender our ancestral right,” he said.
 A similar rally was held in Chandel district, demanding Ms. Kipgen’s resignation and the abrogation of the SoO agreement.
 Manipur has been in the grip of an ethnic conflict between the valley-based Meitei and hill-based Kuki communities since May 2023 that has claimed at least 306 lives while several remain missing. Also, clashes between Kukis and Nagas in the State have led to the death of around 50 people since February this year.
 For the first time since ethnic violence erupted in Manipur in 2023, security forces have taken control of a camp meant to house Kuki-Zo militants under the nearly two-decade-old truce and plan to audit all 14 such camps across the State.
 This rare takeover followed the discovery that only one of the 159 registered cadres was present at the camp, raising questions about compliance with the SoO agreement, which expired on September 4 without renewal.
 The discrepancy raises questions about compliance with one of the central conditions of the agreement that militants covered by it must remain in designated camps and refrain from violence.
 The agreement, formally signed by the Centre, the Manipur government and Kuki-Zo militant groups in August 2008, was intended to suspend hostilities and create conditions for a negotiated political settlement while keeping armed cadres confined to designated camps.
 Its origins date back to 2005, when the Indian Army reached an understanding with Kuki militant groups to suspend operations against each other. The pact covers Kuki-Zo militant groups under two umbrella organisations — the Kuki National Organisation (KNO) and the United People’s Front (UPF).
 Under its ground rules, cadres are required to refrain from violence, remain in designated camps and keep their weapons under prescribed security arrangements.
 The arrangement has been central to the Centre’s efforts to address Kuki-Zo insurgency through negotiations, but its continuation has become increasingly contentious since the outbreak of violence in 2023.
 In February 2024, the Manipur Assembly adopted a resolution seeking abrogation of the agreement. Naga organisations have also demanded its termination, accusing Kuki-Zo militant groups of involvement in violence.
